anchors.title: Lovelace's objection
anchors.story: In her notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine, Ada Lovelace argued the machine could only do what people knew how to order it to perform — it had no power to originate anything on its own.

anchors.title: Turing's machine question
anchors.story: Alan Turing's 1936 work gave a precise model of computation. In 1950 he shifted the public question from definitions of thinking to an operational test of machine intelligence.

source.label: Turing, "On Computable Numbers" (1936); "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" (1950)

anchors.title: Dartmouth names artificial intelligence
anchors.story: The Dartmouth summer research proposal gathered researchers around the claim that aspects of learning and intelligence could be described precisely enough for a machine to simulate them.
